correctness.rationale: For every finite projective plane q>=2, deleting one point leaves connected no-four-cycle incidence graph H; opposite-side radius<=2 cliques remain exactly incident pairs. All surviving point vertices form a simplex; line-side graph misses precisely the edges between q+1 lines formerly meeting at deleted point, but any other line is a cone vertex. The two cover subcomplexes are contractible and meet in H, hence VR<=2(H)≃ΣH≃∨^{q^3−q}S². Naturality of the same cover for G identifies H2 map with inclusion of integral graph cycle lattices. Its quotient injects into the free abelian coordinates of the q+1 deleted edges and has rank q, so the injection is primitive. Independent construction of PG(2,2),PG(2,3) gives 13/25 surviving vertices, 18/48 edges and cycle ranks 6/24. Every scale is inclusive with post-deletion graph distances; no claim about higher scales.

value.rationale: A single deleted landmark is a natural stability perturbation of the highly symmetric point-line metric. The theorem specifies both exact loss q of integral generators and primitive nature of the induced map for all finite projective planes, including non-Desarguesian models; these data can inform filtration comparison and are not determined solely by the original Betti numbers.
